blocks.text: Gate 4A defines how the 324 canonical Era Zero atoms may be composed without approving any particular compound meaning. A lexical compound is a finite connected directed acyclic semantic graph with exactly one explicit semantic head. Every component retains its canonical atomic meaning and generated forms.

Source-grounded realization remains fixed: describing material precedes its semantic head; a no-gap boundary marks modifier attachment; a short gap marks typed argument attachment; and only the semantic head normally receives the compound's external role contour.

Node types: canonical root, approved versioned compound reference, typed open slot, and explicit coordination group. Gate 4A edge types are qualifies (descriptor to described node), fills_role (typed argument to predicate or relation), and member_of (member to an all-of, any-of, or exactly-one group).

The role inventory covers actor, source, cause, experiencer, bearer, predicate, target, result, destination, instrument, material, location, environment, condition, and persistent condition. Core low, middle, high, and sustained-background register mappings remain unchanged.

Modifier and argument targets are explicit; adjacency never overrides the graph. Nested references must be versioned and acyclic. Multiple independent assertions are not lexical compounds and must wait for the later utterance IR.

Canonical compound identity is derived from a normalized semantic payload containing the architecture version, head, nodes, edges, and lexical constraints. Presentation metadata, English glosses, runtime state, contour, register, and absolute pitch are excluded from the content identity.

Runtime [0], [1], or [2]/num belongs to an utterance occurrence and is never stored as part of a lexical compound identity. Changing a compound's head, graph, role binding, scope, slot type, or lexical constraints requires a new definition version and migration; approved entries may be deprecated or superseded but never silently rewritten.
